column.text: Bitcoin's spot ETF bid is the one signal worth respecting, and it isn't fully counted yet. Wednesday's BTC flow printed +$524.8M, but issuers are still reporting, so treat that figure as provisional. The seven-day net sits at +$911.7M, meaning institutions have been buying into weakness rather than chasing strength. The rest of the complex is not following. Ethereum's Wednesday inflow of +$14.9M is also partial, against a seven-day net of −$349.2M. Solana's seven-day net of −$33.6M tells the same story. Alts are being sold while BTC gets bid, which is rotation, not a rally. Underneath, stablecoin supply has contracted to $305B. Fed rate-cut odds at 88% say the macro backdrop is supportive, but capital already on-chain is leaving, and those two signals are pulling against each other. Fear & Greed reads 68, Greed, so the crowd has already leaned in. Our regime is RISK_OFF. A down-trending tape is not a short by itself. A short needs a mechanism we can point to in the printed blocks, and below conviction 7 it trades at half size. Continuation longs need real proof: rising open interest with price, a reclaim of the 20-day MA, or a negative-funding squeeze. Counter-trend longs need clear exhaustion and a catalyst, never a reflexive dip-buy. Dollar liquidity is flat, so price structure decides. Watch whether BTC's inflows hold once Wednesday's issuers finish reporting, and whether stablecoin supply stops shrinking.
